input.question: Why do we forget our dreams after waking up?
input.ground_truth: They aren't important to you. If you write them down or even mentally reevaluate them before you get out of bed or reorient yourself, you'll retain them better, but on a base level your brain prioritizes remembering real sense-data and clearing out or ignoring your "imagination."

Question: Why do we forget our dreams after waking up?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your brain is like a little toy box. When you go to sleep, your brain plays with lots of fun toys (those are your dreams!). But when you wake up, your brain puts most of those toys away and gets ready for the day. That’s why you often can’t remember your dreams—they got put back in the toy box, and you didn’t pay attention when you put them away.

So, you forget your dreams because your brain is busy thinking about other things, like breakfast or playing!
